about: The fluidity scenarios scripts/fluidity/run.mjs runs, each held to its budgets file (Fluidity budgets #6; PLATFORM-LEAD, 17 Oct 2026). A programme registers its own here: a script beside this file, its budgets file, what it needs and the CPU slowdowns it runs at.

A script takes --base <url> --cpu <n> --runs <n> --budgets <file> --result <file>, writes { "checks": [rows] } to --result, rows as budgets.mjs's check() makes them, and exits 1 when an enforced budget is missed. covers names the budgets' scenario fields it measures (a budget's scenario must be covered here: app/fluidityBudgets.test.ts).

needs: build (a production build in .next, no server), fixtures (a production server, every answer faked: nothing leaves the machine), demo (a production server with the live demo's data, read only). gate: run in the integrator's full gate after its build; the rest run nightly and before a release, on a quieter machine, as medians.

surfaces.mjs (FLUIDITY-LEAD, 20 Oct 2026) is the one harness the work, tables, calendar-fixtures and shell scenarios share: --only names its group in surfaces/, and cpu 4 runs it as a phone (390 x 844, touch). Times count only from P-cores (heavy.sh --pcore); every run records its load, CPUs, clock and temperature.
